audits.title: Using audit to monitor and improve the quality of anaesthesia for caesarean section.
audits.setting: Maternity unit, district general hospital (Inverclyde Royal, Greenock)

cycle1.result: General anaesthesia in 58.0% of emergency and 45.5% of elective sections (53.0% overall); 25.3% had anaesthetic complications or side-effects; 90.3% satisfied.

audits.intervention: Findings presented to the multidisciplinary team and changes to anaesthetic practice introduced

cycle2.result: General anaesthesia fell to 23.8% (P < 0.05); complications or side-effects 17.2%; satisfaction maintained.

audits.citation: Simmons M, Bowie P, Heatley L. Using audit to monitor and improve the quality of anaesthesia for caesarean section. Health Bull (Edinb). 1999;57(5):338-343. PMID: 12811881.

audits.title: Prospective multidisciplinary audit of obstetric general anaesthesia in a district general hospital.
audits.standard: Royal College of Anaesthetists recommended general anaesthesia rate for caesarean section
audits.setting: Cheltenham General Hospital, district general hospital labour ward

cycle1.result: Potential serious shortfalls in communication and teamworking; insufficient information to assess appropriateness of indication for general anaesthesia.

audits.intervention: Recommendations to improve communication channels between labour ward personnel.
audits.other_findings: A reduction in use of general anaesthesia coincided with the recommendations, but no figures are given.
audits.citation: Shroff R, Thompson AC, McCrum A, Rees SG. Prospective multidisciplinary audit of obstetric general anaesthesia in a district general hospital. J Obstet Gynaecol. 2004;24(6):641-646. doi:10.1080/01443610400007877. PMID: 16147603.

audits.title: A prospective audit of regional anaesthesia failure in 5080 Caesarean sections.
audits.standard: Royal College of Anaesthetists targets for conversion of regional to general anaesthesia: 1% for elective and 3% for emergency Caesarean section
audits.setting: Department of Anaesthesia, St Michael's Hospital, Bristol

cycle1.result: Conversion of regional to general anaesthesia 0.8% for elective and 4.9% for emergency Caesarean section; 20% in category 1 Caesarean section. 8% of women had general anaesthesia overall (primary plus conversion).

audits.other_findings: Failure to achieve a pain-free operation was 6% with spinals, 24% with epidural top-up and 18% with combined spinal-epidural. Serious adverse incidents were 1:126 with general and 1:501 with regional anaesthesia.
audits.citation: Kinsella SM. A prospective audit of regional anaesthesia failure in 5080 Caesarean sections. Anaesthesia. 2008;63(8):822-832. doi:10.1111/j.1365-2044.2008.05499.x. PMID: 18547291.

audits.title: Conversion of regional to general anaesthesia at caesarean section: increasing the use of regional anaesthesia through continuous prospective audit.
audits.standard: Royal College of Anaesthetists standards for regional anaesthesia and conversion rates at caesarean section

cycle1.result: Retrospective audit showed 9.4% conversion to general anaesthesia for caesarean sections in women with epidural catheters in situ.

audits.intervention: Continuous prospective audit of anaesthetic technique and conversions.

cycle2.result: Neuraxial rates elective 95.3% (2004) to 98.2% (2007), emergency 82.3% (2004) to 85.7% (2007); conversion elective 0.8% (2004) to 0% (2007), emergency 7.8% (2004) to 5.4% (2007).

audits.other_findings: Improvements in all but category 1 caesarean sections; authors suggest RCoA standards become category-specific.
audits.citation: Rafi MA, Arfeen Z, Misra U. Conversion of regional to general anaesthesia at caesarean section: increasing the use of regional anaesthesia through continuous prospective audit. Int J Obstet Anesth. 2010;19(2):179-182. doi:10.1016/j.ijoa.2009.08.008. PMID: 20199859.

audits.title: Blood pressure management for caesarean delivery under spinal anaesthesia: a UK multi-centre audit (2023).
audits.standard: NICE: systolic BP maintained ≥90% of baseline; international consensus prophylactic phenylephrine via rate-controlled device at 25-50 μg/min
audits.setting: Multi-centre prospective audit across West Midlands hospitals

cycle1.result: SBP ≥90% baseline in 9.1%; 80-90% in 65.0%; below 80% in 25.9%; consensus phenylephrine regimen compliance 37.6%

audits.other_findings: Phenylephrine first-line in 91%, via rate-controlled device in 73.8%; intra-operative nausea 24.9% and vomiting 8.4%.
audits.citation: Blackburn J, Yates EJ, Jarvis MS, Small CL, Kerr J, Patel J, et al.. Blood pressure management for caesarean delivery under spinal anaesthesia: a UK multi-centre audit (2023). Int J Obstet Anesth. 2025;62:104352. doi:10.1016/j.ijoa.2025.104352. PMID: 40184831.

audits.title: Obstetric anaesthesia for caesarean section in Central Europe: a prospective population-weighted binational audit (OBAAMA-COV Study).
audits.standard: Neuraxial anaesthesia preferred; general anaesthesia rate as a quality indicator (European standards)
audits.setting: 94 maternity units in the Czech Republic and Slovakia, national audit

cycle1.result: General anaesthesia 33.9% (Czech Republic) and 31.3% (Slovakia); elective 23.0% and 24.9%; emergency 45.4% and 36.8%.

audits.other_findings: Maternal preference was the leading indication for general anaesthesia in elective cases; rates plateaued since 2015.
audits.citation: Bláha J, Nosková P, Seidlová D, Grochová M, Klozová R, Firment J, et al.. Obstetric anaesthesia for caesarean section in Central Europe: a prospective population-weighted binational audit (OBAAMA-COV Study). J Anesth Analg Crit Care. 2026. doi:10.1186/s44158-026-00435-2. PMID: 42421119.
